We're preparing our SOC 2 evidence packet and need a consolidated vulnerability management deliverable from Redwood covering:

- Scan cadence (auth/unauth, agent vs. network) and retention of scan artifacts
- SLA windows for CVE remediation by severity (P0/P1/P2 definitions and target times)

Peter — thanks for the ask. We can provide a compact evidence packet that should satisfy SOC 2 / SIG reviewers. High-level summary below; attaching the first-pass artifacts (scan-report-20260501.pdf and vm-playbook-summary.pdf).

Key commitments (summary) — Redwood Inference VM playbook
- Scan cadence: authenticated weekly scans for infra and container images, monthly full unauthenticated network scans, and nightly dependency/package vulnerability sweeps.
- SLA windows (by severity):
  - Critical / P0 (remote code execution with active exploit): acknowledge within 2 hours; mitigation plan within 48 hours; target remediation or compensating control within 7 days.
  - High / P1 (privilege escalation, data exposure): acknowledge within 8 hours; mitigation plan within 72 hours; target remediation within 14 days.
  - Medium / P2: acknowledge within 48 hours; remediation target 30 days.
  - Low / P3: triage in routine sprint, target 90 days.
- Ownership & workflow: automated ticket creation in Jira on CVE detection, routed to the owning team per attached cve-ownership-matrix.csv; security leads get an automatic escalation at 72h for P1/P0 and at 14d for P2.
- Evidence retention: raw scan exports retained 12 months, summarized reports retained indefinitely in evidence Drive folder.

We can provide a signed attestation confirming the SLA language above for your binder. If your SOC reviewer needs slight wording changes, we can discuss the exact phrasing we can sign off on.

Next steps:
1) I'll loop in Mina (security engineering) with the ownership matrix and ask her to add the automation and ticket templates.
2) If Acme wants a one-page signed attestation, confirm whether the Attestation should be to Acme specifically or a general SOC2 evidence statement — we can produce both.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

On Mon, May 4, 2026 at 10:02 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> We can provide a compact evidence packet that should satisfy SOC 2 / SIG reviewers.

Thanks — adding technical detail for the packet and operational playbook. I've attached the cve-ownership-matrix.csv and included a short checklist below that maps to what your auditor will typically look for.

Operational playbook (excerpts) — Redwood security engineering
- Detection: weekly authenticated scans (Nessus-based) with nightly SCA (software composition analysis) against container images. Monthly external unauthenticated network scans.
- Triage & classification: automated CVE enrichment (NVD + vendor advisories) -> severity normalized to Redwood taxonomy (Critical/High/Medium/Low).
- Ticketing & remediation: automated Jira ticket created with labels: severity, affected-service, rollout-window. Ticket template includes rollback steps and mitigations.
- Escalation matrix:
  - P0/P1: owners notified via PagerDuty; security on-call notified immediately; secondary escalation to LAUNCH leadership if not acknowledged within SLA ack window.
  - P2: notified to owners + security channel; auto-escalation to manager at 14 days.
- Verification: post-remediation rescans for the fixed asset; evidence attached to Jira and copied to evidence Drive folder.
- Metrics & reporting: weekly VM dashboard (open CVEs by severity, MTTR by severity, backlog age).

Attachments included: cve-ownership-matrix.csv (CSV); I've also uploaded a ready-to-sign attestation draft to the evidence Drive link (see below). If Acme needs vendor-specific wording, point to the exact clause and we will respond.

Mina Haddad
Security Engineer, Vulnerability Management
Redwood Inference
